passA.contextIsolation: This fresh Pass A used only the exact allowlisted source chain and accessed no legacy assessment, other scoring pass, adjudication, ledger, reliability analysis, production assessment, other debate, or other agent output.

passB.contextIsolation: This fresh Pass B task used only the exhaustive allowlist above and accessed neither legacy assessment material nor Pass A output or rationale.

burdens.description: Show that physical reality has an ultimately personal, transcendent creator rather than being brute, necessary, or grounded impersonally.
burdens.successCriteria: Give a defensible route from features of physical reality to a personal transcendent cause and answer the principal rival-grounding objections raised in the exchange.

burdens.description: Show that classical theism supplies objective meaning and moral obligation in a way the alternatives do not.
burdens.successCriteria: Explain both the grounding and normative authority of meaning and duty, and answer challenges about arbitrariness, coercion, and independently accessible value.

burdens.description: Defend classical-theist epistemic controls against rival mystical and pluralist accounts.
burdens.successCriteria: Provide public or otherwise discriminating grounds for the classical account and identify non-question-begging defeaters for competing experience-based claims.

burdens.speaker: Jessica Frazier
burdens.description: Develop an impersonal or non-dual account of cosmic unity, order, emergence, and value that is not reducible to classical theism.
burdens.successCriteria: State the alternative's explanatory structure and show how it accounts for relevant features without merely renaming them divine.

burdens.speaker: Philip Goff
burdens.description: Defend a consciousness-involving, limited-God alternative that accommodates existence, fine-tuning, mystical experience, and suffering.
burdens.successCriteria: Connect the experience and metaphysics through an intelligible inference, avoid contradiction, and explain how divine limitation addresses suffering.

burdens.speaker: Joe Folley
burdens.description: Challenge the necessity of classical theism for meaning and normativity while maintaining an appropriately agnostic posture on cosmic origins.
burdens.successCriteria: Distinguish kinds of meaning, explain constraints on valuation or obligation, and identify what theistic authority adds without treating uncertainty as a contrary proof.

burdens.description: Test whether the pro case establishes classical theism rather than only some cause, ground, value source, or religious interpretation.
burdens.successCriteria: Expose an unearned inference from shared or ambiguous evidence to the specifically classical-theist conclusion.

sections.title: Cosmic explanation and comparative scope
sections.weightRationale: The motion centrally asks where physical reality came from and which worldview explains it; this section therefore receives the largest weight without treating Craig's enumerated but mostly undeveloped arguments as six separate successes.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: In the course of my philosophical work, I've defended six arguments for God's existence in support of a positive answer to that question. First, God is the best explanation of why anything at all exists rather than just nothing. Second, God is the best explanation of the absolute beginning of the universe at a point in the finite past.

passA.rationale: Constructive opening: the inference is intelligible and squarely addresses the motion, yet it mostly announces conclusions and refers generally to published defenses. It materially advances P-B1 by naming routes to a creator, but does not complete that burden because the personal-cause bridge and rival comparisons are absent from this span; the later claim that no comparable atheist case exists is also under-supported.

passB.rationale: As a constructive-opening response class, the move is clear and central to P-B1, but it lists conclusions rather than presenting the warranted route to a personal transcendent creator. Its unqualified best-explanation language also outruns what this locked span establishes.

adjudication.rationale: Constructive opening: the locked span is central to P-B1 and clearly names contingency and a finite beginning as routes toward God, but it announces best-explanation conclusions without presenting their premises, comparing rival grounds, or supplying the bridge to a personal transcendent creator. The unqualified comparative claims therefore receive limited warrant and calibration credit within this span.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: The reality of temporal becoming is more evident to us than the reality of the external world because we sense temporal becoming in the inner life of the mind, the thoughts that succeed one another as well as in the external world. So, that's I think a quite hopeless defeater of the argument against the infinitude of the past to try to appeal to this tenseless theory of time.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the span directly addresses the live block-universe component and clearly states its phenomenological basis, but experienced succession does not by itself establish the A-theory or show an infinite past impossible. Calling the defeater hopeless is disproportionate to the offered warrant, and the answer leaves the separate actual-infinity challenge unresolved.

passB.rationale: The full-direct-answer response class engages both parts of the live finite-past challenge with an intelligible experiential warrant. For P-B1, the locked burden consequence is material support for a finite beginning, though not yet for a personal cause. Calling the tenseless reply hopeless and ranking temporal becoming above external-world awareness are insufficiently calibrated.

adjudication.rationale: Full direct answer: the span answers both parts of the audience challenge, treating metaphysical counterintuition as evidence against an actual infinite and inner succession as evidence against a tenseless escape. The analogies and phenomenology provide an intelligible but incomplete warrant, while calling the tenseless defeater hopeless overstates the case. The locked burden consequence is material support for a finite beginning under P-B1, not completion of the further personal-cause inference.

moves.speaker: Jessica Frazier
moves.sourceExcerpt: If we look at everything in the world around us, all these people, we tend to just see the objects, we need to remember to see the connections, the spaces, the continuum, the way in which everything we see is unified in some sense through causes, through space-time relations.

passA.rationale: Relevant counterargument: the relational framing is coherent and genuinely alternative, but observing connectedness does not yet explain the universe or show why the unity is impersonal or non-dual. It advances a necessary part of C-B1 while leaving its explanatory mechanism and the C-B4 comparison with classical theism largely unstated.

passB.rationale: The relevant-counterargument response class offers a coherent non-classical starting frame for C-B1, but unity through relations neither answers Craig's explanatory demand nor yet specifies a grounding mechanism. The named philosophical support remains compressed and the motion-level consequence is incomplete.

moves.speaker: Philip Goff
moves.sourceExcerpt: I'm also very much persuaded by certain traditional arguments for God's existence, kind of like Bill likes, arguments rooted in the need to explain why the universe exists, why it's fine-tuned for life. The problem is though, I'm also completely persuaded by the most discussed argument against God's existence rooted in the need to explain why there's so much suffering in the world.

passA.rationale: Relevant counterargument: the concessive comparison is unusually charitable and coherently separates evidence for some God from evidence for classical omnipotence, although the span asserts rather than develops the suffering argument. It materially advances C-B2 and C-B4 by blocking the inference from cosmological evidence to classical theism, with the limited-God explanation still to be supplied elsewhere.

passB.rationale: The relevant-counterargument response class charitably separates evidence for some God from the classical package. For C-B2 and shared C-B4, the locked burden consequence is that cosmological agreement does not establish an unlimited classical God; however, the span merely calls standard suffering replies unsatisfying and does not develop the comparison.

moves.speaker: Joe Folley
moves.sourceExcerpt: There's an attempt to use principles that are considered to be justified in order to trace something in the Kalam case, trace something back to the beginning of the universe and infer something about it. And then through the second stage we establish that cause has various properties and it begins to look like God.

passA.rationale: Relevant counterargument: the reconstruction is clear, coherent, and highly charitable, but the actual objection about exporting in-universe principles occurs after the locked endpoint and cannot repair this move. Inside the scored span Folley identifies the inferential architecture without exposing a failed premise, so responsiveness and burden impact remain limited despite strong accuracy.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class is notably fair to the pro case, but the locked span ends before Folley supplies his extrapolation objection or completes the second-stage reconstruction. It therefore offers useful orientation without yet discharging C-B3 or testing the classical conclusion under C-B4.

sections.title: Creator, creation, and non-dual alternatives
sections.weightRationale: The exchange directly tests whether explanatory dependence entails ontological separation, emanation, or overlap, an important discriminator among the represented worldviews.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: There's a creator-creation distinction since the creation is material in space and time, but the creator is an immaterial, spiritual, transcendent reality that has brought the physical world into being. In this case, we would want to say, I think, that God is what you've called a self-natured being.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the ontology is clear and responds at the relevant point by distinguishing kinds of being rather than denying dependence. It materially advances P-B1 by stating the creator-creation distinction needed for a transcendent source, but does not establish within the span that all physical reality is contingent or that the necessary ground is personal.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class directly states the ontology the pro case requires but does not yet warrant why causal dependence entails this sharp separation. For P-B1, the locked burden consequence is a clear personal-transcendent creator thesis rather than mere cosmic unity, although the thesis is asserted more than established.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: If one circle of the Venn diagram represents everything that is timeless, immaterial, spaceless, necessarily existent, and the other circle represents everything that is temporal, material, contingent, then they cannot overlap. Those are self-contradictory. So, the area of overlap is a contradiction.

passA.rationale: Topic shift or weaker substitution: the conditional contradiction is lucid if the two circles have Craig's stipulated exhaustive properties, but Goff's stated model placed a timeless, uncreated conscious core within the universe rather than defining the whole universe as contingent. The move therefore defeats a materially weaker property assignment and does not directly test whether Goff's proposed core is coherent.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class states a crisp conditional contradiction, but it assumes the entire universe has the second set of properties that Goff's proposal is positioned to deny. That unargued property assignment weakens coherence and charity, so the move tests C-B2 without decisively defeating it.

adjudication.rationale: Topic shift or weaker substitution: Craig's conditional is logically clear if one circle is wholly necessary, timeless, and immaterial while the other is wholly contingent, temporal, and material. Goff had instead located a necessary, timeless conscious core within the universe, so assigning the whole universe the contrary properties attacks a materially weaker version of C-B2. The response therefore stays below the 49 ceiling despite its crisp conditional structure.

moves.speaker: Jessica Frazier
moves.sourceExcerpt: There's whatever creates the world. If you're a Thomist, they're the powers in God, the concepts in God that unfold and generate. And then there's the parts of God which are under it. And if you're a physicist, there's the Big Bang and the whatever it is that's generating space-time.

passA.rationale: Relevant counterargument: the comparison usefully shows that a generative level and a supporting condition need not be described in Craig's preferred vocabulary. However, its shifting references to powers, parts, the Big Bang, and an unspecified generator blur distinct relations and do not yet establish a non-dual alternative or answer why the ground should be impersonal.

passB.rationale: The relevant-counterargument response class shows that layered explanation is not unique to classical creation, but its analogies blur importantly different kinds of dependence and do not explain Frazier's own alternative. It is topical for C-B1 and C-B4 without answering why the specific pro inference fails.

moves.speaker: Jessica Frazier
moves.sourceExcerpt: Emanationism gets given lots of different ontological sort of play outs, right? I mean, even Aquinas will say creation ex nihilo never means that God creates the world and then he's like, ‘That was great. I'm going away.’ In fact, that was a heresy. The universe, all that the divine creates, is always sustained.

passA.rationale: Relevant counterargument: the historical-theological example accurately narrows the distance between creation and emanation by stressing ongoing dependence. It does not answer Craig's necessary-versus-contingent distinction, since continuous sustaining is compatible with ontological separation, so the move provides useful contrary context without resolving the live issue.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class narrows Craig's contrast by identifying genuine common dependence language, and it does so without claiming that Aquinas simply endorsed emanation. It leaves unresolved whether continuous sustaining is ontological overlap, so it advances C-B1 and C-B4 without completing them.

adjudication.rationale: Relevant counterargument: Frazier accurately uses Aquinas's continuous sustaining to show that classical creation is not a deistic one-off event and thereby narrows the contrast with emanation. The move does not answer Craig's central necessary-versus-contingent distinction or establish ontological overlap, so it supplies relevant contrary context without resolving the live claim and remains below the 69 responsiveness ceiling.

moves.speaker: Philip Goff
moves.sourceExcerpt: Think of a Venn diagram where you've got the bit of God that's wholly other, that's completely separate from the universe; the bit of the universe or the nature of the universe which is wholly separate to God; and then the bit in the middle, like a Venn diagram.

passA.rationale: Relevant counterargument: the model is understandable and supplies a genuine third option between strict separation and identity, but the diagram is an illustration rather than a warrant for compatible shared properties. It materially advances C-B2 by stating the central overlap structure and C-B4 by contesting classical exclusivity, while leaving the metaphysical basis of the overlap underdeveloped.

passB.rationale: The relevant-counterargument response class offers a recoverable alternative to strict identity or separation, central to Goff's C-B2 position, but the locked span does not explain how one entity or region can instantiate the proposed cross-category relation. The experiential claim is asserted rather than independently warranted.

moves.speaker: Philip Goff
moves.sourceExcerpt: I wouldn't define the physical universe as essentially contingent then. I think most of it is, but I think there's something at the core of the universe, there's something at the core of you, Bill, and at the core of me that is necessary, timeless, uncreated. And that's where the overlap is.

passA.rationale: Full direct answer: Goff resolves Craig's stated contradiction by rejecting the premise that every part of the universe bears contingent, temporal properties, so compatibility is restored at the exact point of attack. This materially advances C-B2 by preserving the limited-God overlap model, though compatibility alone does not provide evidence that such a necessary conscious core exists.

passB.rationale: The full-direct-answer response class resolves Craig's stated contradiction at its decisive premise by denying the universal property assignment, rather than accepting incompatible properties. For C-B2, the locked burden consequence is preservation of internal compatibility for the overlap model; evidence that such a core exists remains thin.

sections.title: Mystical experience and public warrant
sections.weightRationale: Mystical experience supplies Goff's principal evidence and generates sustained replies about cognitive content, defeaters, and public accessibility; it is tied with cosmic explanation for highest weight.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: Once one starts appealing to these sorts of mystical experiences to justify your worldview, it seems to me that you've lost all controls on objectivity and on truth. I too could claim what you would probably call a mystical experience, namely, at the age of sixteen, after six months of the most intense soul-searching I've ever been through, I was spiritually born again.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the competing experience directly raises underdetermination, but this span does not yet state the historical controls Craig later offers or explain why his experience is epistemically better. It materially advances P-B3 by demanding a discriminator that Goff's inference needs, while leaving the pro side's own public-control burden only partially discharged.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class properly raises underdetermination by rival experiences, but this locked span ends before Craig supplies the promised public controls for his own interpretation. It advances P-B3 by posing a discriminating-evidence challenge without yet establishing asymmetrical grounds for classical theism.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: How do you know, Philip, that your mystical experience was not an experience of the orthodox God? How do you know that it was this indescribable, self-contradictory, strange God, especially since there doesn't seem to be any cognitive content to differentiate it? Maybe you had an experience of the orthodox God.

passA.rationale: Full direct answer: although phrased interrogatively, the move resolves Goff's strongest live inference by showing that his locked evidence supplies no content discriminating his model from orthodox theism. It materially advances P-B3 and C-B4 by exposing the unearned worldview selection, although calling Goff's God self-contradictory and strange goes beyond what this underdetermination argument establishes.

passB.rationale: The full-direct-answer response class defeats the specific experiential inference unless Goff can identify discriminating content, because the diagnosis itself resolves the burden at its decisive premise. For P-B3, the locked burden consequence is a decisive underdetermination objection to the rival interpretation. Calling the alternative self-contradictory and strange adds an unsupported, less charitable characterization.

moves.speaker: Philip Goff
moves.sourceExcerpt: Neurophysiologically, what it looks like it's doing is suppressing, stopping neural activity, not creating new neural activity like you imagine in a hallucination. Imagine my mind is a light bulb wrapped in cotton wool. The cotton wool is what's particular to me, Philip Goff, and the light bulb is this pure consciousness.

passA.rationale: Constructive opening: the metaphor makes the proposed filter model recoverable and directly serves Goff's experiential burden. Yet reduced neural activity does not by itself discriminate revelation from altered construction, and the hallucination contrast is asserted without representative data or rival mechanisms, leaving the crucial disclosure inference substantially under-warranted.

passB.rationale: As a constructive-opening response class, the move makes Goff's C-B2 filter model intelligible, but neural suppression alone does not distinguish disclosure from altered or degraded cognition. The source and representativeness of the neuroscience are not developed, and the metaphor carries more inferential weight than it can support.

moves.speaker: Philip Goff
moves.sourceExcerpt: You can't get outside of your consciousness and check whether it's corresponding to reality. So, what do you do? You've just got to decide which experiences seem most evident. And anybody who's had the experience I had—it is more compelling than anything in ordinary experience, far more compelling. Also, with this particular substance, it is very uniform.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the appeal to experiential seeming addresses Craig's demand for a starting point and adds uniformity as a possible reliability marker. It leaves necessary differences between ordinary perception and a drug-induced state unresolved, provides no error-rate or rival-explanation comparison, and moves too quickly from compelling phenomenology to metaphysical truth.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class explains why the experience can be prima facie evidence for Goff, but it does not answer relevant-difference or defeater questions separating induced mystical experience from ordinary perception. Intensity and uniformity are asserted broadly and do not by themselves warrant the specific metaphysics required by C-B2.

moves.speaker: Joe Folley
moves.sourceExcerpt: I don't quite know what an unstructured cognitive content looks like. It seems like the really cool thing and the useful thing about cognitive content is that we can put it in structures and thus it can enter the public arena of discourse. It seems like cognitive content, at least as far as I can tell, would imply structure.

passA.rationale: Diagnostic question: the move precisely exposes the missing bridge between ineffable seeming and publicly assessable content without pretending to prove an alternative metaphysics. It is maximally responsive for a diagnosis that does not itself settle whether private content can exist, and its restrained formulation accurately targets Goff's stated account rather than another con speaker's theory.

passB.rationale: The diagnostic-question response class sharply exposes a missing bridge between ineffable seeming and publicly assessable inference, while explicitly allowing that Folley's premise may be wrong. Because this critiques Goff rather than advancing Folley's C-B3 meaning burden or directly testing the pro case under C-B4, its locked burden relevance is limited.

adjudication.rationale: Diagnostic question: Folley precisely exposes the missing bridge between unstructured cognitive content and material that can enter public discourse, while conceding that his premise may be wrong. The diagnosis does not itself settle whether private content can exist, so responsiveness is capped at 74. Judged against Folley's C-B3 and genuinely shared C-B4 rather than Goff's C-B2, criticizing an allied speaker's mystical account has only limited locked-burden relevance.

moves.speaker: Jessica Frazier
moves.sourceExcerpt: You might have to speak to experiences that go beyond the usual. The first time as a kid I experienced what it was like when the plane dives and you feel weightlessness, it was a new experience. It didn't mean it was not a veridical experience. It was just an unusual thing.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the counterexample cleanly defeats any inference from unfamiliarity alone to falsity and remains carefully limited. It does not show that Goff's experience tracks its claimed metaphysical object or supply a discriminator among interpretations, so it offers a strong local correction without completing Frazier's own C-B1 account or Goff's C-B2 burden.

passB.rationale: The topic-shift-or-weaker-substitution response class competently rebuts the weaker claim that unusual phenomenology is automatically false, but Craig's strongest live objection concerned discriminating cognitive content, not mere unfamiliarity. The careful limited conclusion does little for Frazier's own C-B1 account or shared C-B4.

adjudication.rationale: Partial direct answer: Frazier answers part of the live challenge by pointing to consistent reports, recoverable what-it-is-like content, and the valid distinction between unusual experience and fabricated experience. She does not provide public discrimination among rival metaphysical interpretations or show that Goff's experience tracks its claimed object, leaving necessary components unresolved. Judged against her C-B1 and shared C-B4 rather than Goff's theory, the move is a useful local defense with limited burden completion.

sections.title: Objective and subjective meaning
sections.weightRationale: Meaning is explicit in the motion and opening cases, but the discussion concerns several distinct senses and is less directly developed than origins or mystical warrant.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: Many atheists have recognized that if God does not exist, then our lives are ultimately meaningless. For no matter what we do, it really doesn't matter because everything winds up the same regardless. You can try to make up a meaning to your life, but that's purely subjective. That's just pretending that your life has meaning.

passA.rationale: Constructive opening: the move directly addresses meaning in the motion and clearly contrasts objective with subjective significance. Its conclusion depends on an undefended bridge from temporal finitude or equal final outcomes to present meaninglessness, and describing created meaning as mere pretending caricatures the constrained, agent-relative accounts later articulated by Folley.

passB.rationale: As a constructive-opening response class, the move squarely states P-B2's meaning thesis, but the inference from temporal finitude to lack of objective significance is missing. It treats subjective meaning as pretense without comparing rival accounts and overgeneralizes about atheistic life, creating distinct coherence and calibration defects.

adjudication.rationale: Constructive opening: the move squarely addresses the motion's meaning question and Craig's adopted P-B2 burden, so it is not penalized for lacking a prior opponent move. Its inference from eventual extinction or equal final outcomes to present objective meaninglessness is unstated, and describing self-created meaning as pretense overgeneralizes beyond what the span warrants.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: I'm talking about meaning in an objective sense, not a subjective sense. Is there an objective meaning to human existence? And it seems to me to have an objective meaning, we need this external transcendent reality, God, to tell us what the objective meaning in life is. The meaning of life is to glorify God and to know him and enjoy him forever.

passA.rationale: Relevant counterargument: the move helpfully sharpens the target from felt fulfillment to objective purpose, but it reasserts rather than warrants the necessity of a divine teller and does not answer Folley's plurality of meanings. The stipulated purpose therefore advances P-B2 only topically and leaves both its grounding and worthiness bridge open.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class clarifies which meaning claim is at issue but mostly restates it. It neither answers Folley's plural senses nor supplies the bridge from external assignment to objective worth, so the span remains central to P-B2 while its warrant and responsiveness are materially incomplete.

moves.speaker: Joe Folley
moves.sourceExcerpt: We hear ‘what is the meaning of life’ and we are necessarily fixed into a kind of reified view of the question. We think, ‘Okay, there must be this thing called meaning out there and we need to find it.’ If we look at the way that we use the term meaning, it seems to refer to different related but ultimately distinct things.

passA.rationale: Justified reframe: Folley explains why the unitary demand is malformed and redirects evaluation to distinct senses rather than merely changing subjects. This materially advances C-B3 and C-B4 by preventing Craig's objective-versus-subjective dichotomy from settling every kind of meaning; empirical or conceptual support for the full taxonomy remains compressed in the span.

passB.rationale: The justified-reframe response class explains why the unitary question is malformed and answers the corrected issue with a plural taxonomy and explicit concessions. For C-B3 and C-B4, the locked burden consequence is that Craig must establish which kind of meaning uniquely requires God, rather than infer a single objective property from the word alone.

moves.speaker: Jessica Frazier
moves.sourceExcerpt: If God says, ‘What I really want you to do is kick puppies, and if you do it really well, you'll get to heaven,’ your job is to say, ‘That's stupid. Even though you're God and you created me, I'm not going to do that. I have access to higher values.’ Just because you're created for something doesn't mean you have to value it.

passA.rationale: Full direct answer: the counterexample isolates and defeats the missing inference from creator-given telos to worthy objective meaning. It materially advances C-B1 and C-B4 by showing that creation alone cannot complete P-B2, though it assumes rather than grounds access to higher values and does not address Craig's later appeal to God's necessarily good nature.

passB.rationale: The full-direct-answer response class targets the decisive bridge from creator-assigned telos to worthy meaning and shows that creation alone is insufficient. For Frazier's C-B1 and shared C-B4, the locked burden consequence is that independently accessible higher value must adjudicate divine purposes, though the counterexample does not itself ground that value.

moves.speaker: Joe Folley
moves.sourceExcerpt: It's clearly not arbitrary in the sense that you can't choose to find anything meaningful. Even if we take a radically extreme subjectivist position on meaning, there are still broad limitations on what you can create. If you're a naturalist, then there are still going to be a limited number of things that most humans would be able to value.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the psychological constraint directly answers Craig's charge that created meaning is arbitrary in the sense of freely invented, while candidly allowing unacceptable options within the range. It does not establish stance-independent significance or resolve conflicts among constrained valuations, so the central arbitrariness reply succeeds without completing C-B3.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class directly rebuts arbitrariness understood as unconstrained choice, while leaving Craig's distinct claims about objectivity and eventual extinction unresolved. For C-B3, the locked burden consequence is a psychologically constrained account of valuation, though no common normative standard for conflict resolution is established.

sections.title: Moral value, obligation, and authority
sections.weightRationale: Objective moral obligation is one of Craig's six stated arguments and receives extended, direct engagement about value, oughtness, prudence, and authority.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: Objectivity is not enough by itself to have objective moral values. We need some sort of oughtness: I ought to do this; I ought not to do that. This is a matter of moral duties. Moral duties arise from imperatives issued by a qualified authority. And God, as the paradigmatic good, is qualified to issue such moral commands to us.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the move directly develops Folley's agency point while correcting a merely coercive account through the qualified-authority condition. It materially advances P-B2 by supplying separate grounds for value and oughtness, but leaves the key warrant that a creator's commands generate categorical obligation defended mainly by assertion rather than a comparison with constitutivist or other realist alternatives.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class uses Folley's distinction constructively and avoids reducing authority to enforcement alone. For P-B2, the locked burden consequence is an explicit proposed ground of moral oughtness in good divine command. The span does not yet justify why authoritative imperatives generate moral rather than merely institutional or prudential reasons.

moves.speaker: William Lane Craig
moves.sourceExcerpt: What happens when your moral duty contradicts what prudence tells you to do? Self-interest and morality often come head-on into conflict. Theism provides a basis for doing your moral duty even at the expense of self-interest, and therefore following your moral obligations over your prudential interests. That's one more practical argument in support of a theistic perspective.

passA.rationale: Partial direct answer: the distinction correctly resists reducing morality to prudence, but the conclusion that theism supports anti-prudential duty is not connected to a mechanism in the span and sits uneasily with the immediately discussed reward-and-punishment framework. It remains relevant to P-B2 while leaving the normativity bridge substantially asserted.

passB.rationale: The partial-direct-answer response class directly resists reducing theism's moral force to prudence, but the locked span does not explain how theism supplies non-prudential motivation or authority. Because an afterlife can align ultimate prudence with duty, the stated contrast is underdeveloped and advances P-B2 only modestly.

moves.speaker: Jessica Frazier
moves.sourceExcerpt: Hinduism says there are moral structures. If you're in the world and you're a consciousness and you're interacting with other consciousness, you have moral responsibilities. And since you are and I am and we all are here, we have those responsibilities. Hinduism is extremely invested in understanding what's called dharma, the structure of how the world around us works.

passA.rationale: Constructive opening: judged against Frazier's own C-B1 rather than another con theory, this accurately states a positive rival source of moral structure. It materially advances C-B1 and C-B4 by denying that punishment or creator fiat is necessary, but the span does not explain how conscious interaction generates categorical duties or adjudicates competing dharmic claims.

passB.rationale: As a constructive-opening response class, the move supplies a positive rival rather than merely denying theism. For C-B1 and shared C-B4, the locked burden consequence is that moral responsibility can arise from conscious relations and world structure without punitive command. The structure and its authority are asserted rather than explained.

moves.speaker: Joe Folley
moves.sourceExcerpt: The mere objectivity of value seems to be underselling the strength of theism here. The Platonic good is a little bit toothless. The advantage of theism isn't necessarily in the mere objectivity of values. It's in the presence of an enforcer of values. That doesn't have anything to do with objectivity at all.

passA.rationale: Constructive opening: judged against Folley's agnostic C-B3, the distinction is clear and concessive about a practical theistic advantage without granting objectivity. It materially advances C-B3 and C-B4 by showing that enforcement and moral truth are different achievements, although it initially compresses theism into enforcement and does not yet explain non-theistic obligation.

passB.rationale: As a constructive-opening response class, the move precisely separates metaethical objectivity from prudential enforcement and makes a strong concession. For C-B3 and shared C-B4, the locked burden consequence is that divine power may improve compliance without proving values objective or classical theism necessary; the motivational premise remains conceptually argued rather than independently supported.

adjudication.rationale: Constructive opening: Folley carefully distinguishes stance-independent value from enforcement and openly grants that a personal divine enforcer gives theism a practical advantage over a toothless Platonic good. Judged against his agnostic C-B3 and shared C-B4, the locked burden consequence is that improved compliance does not itself establish objective value or the necessity of classical theism. The concession supports high charity, although the motivational premise remains conceptually argued rather than independently evidenced.

moves.speaker: Philip Goff
moves.sourceExcerpt: David Hume has this idea that all fundamental life goals are on a par. Reason is the slave of the passions. I just think that can't be true. Imagine someone whose fundamental life goal is counting blades of grass, and they don't enjoy it, they get no pleasure from it. That's just their fundamental life goal.
